rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Quraysh made journeys to Yemen and Busra; in summer they went to Taif for water and shade, and in winter to Mecca for commerce and other needs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رحلة إلى اليمن، ورحلة إلى بصرى.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He takes the singular journey to mean the two seasonal journeys, using singular wording to avoid ambiguity, and supports this usage with poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وأراد رحلتي الشتاء والصيف، فأفرد لأمن الإلباس

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh allows this singular-for-dual usage only as poetic necessity, as in the cited valley poem.
rows.anchor: وهذا عند سيبويه لا يجوز إلا في الضرورة

rows.speaker: النقاش وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says Quraysh had four journeys, while Ibn Atiyya calls that claim rejected.
rows.anchor: وقال النقاش: كانت لهم أربع رحل. قال ابن عطية: وهذا قول مردود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the four-journey view should not be rejected: four brothers secured Quraysh trade routes to Syria, Ethiopia, Yemen, and Persia.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يرد، فإن أصحاب الإيلاف كانوا أربعة إخوة وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers were called protectors; Quraysh traders traveled under their guarantee and no one attacked them.
rows.anchor: فكان هؤلاء يسمون المجيرين، فتختلف تجر قريش إلى الأمصار

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: He explains ilaf as a form of protected tenancy, which makes four journeys plausible across the regions guarded by the brothers.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: الإيلاف شبه الإجارة بالخفارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rihlah is a generic singular that can denote one journey or several.
rows.anchor: فتكون رحلة هنا اسم جنس يصلح للواحد ولأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their journeys is apposition to Quraysh's ilaf; the broad term is specified by its object to magnify the blessing of the protected journey.
rows.anchor: وإيلافهم بدل من لإيلاف قريش، أطلق المبدل منه وقيد البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This House is the Kaaba, whose protection was established in the preceding sura; min gives causation, since God fed them against hunger.
rows.anchor: هو الكعبة، وتمكن هنا هذا اللفظ لتقدم حمايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca was uncultivated and exposed to hunger and fear; God's grace answered Abraham's supplication and brought its produce.
rows.anchor: كانوا قطانا ببلد غير ذي زرع عرضة للجوع والخوف لولا لطف الله تعالى بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh were privileged among Arabs: wherever they settled, people protected them as residents of God's House, while others remained afraid.
rows.anchor: فضلهم على العرب بكونهم يأمنون حيث ما حلوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret being secured from fear as protection from leprosy, saying no leper was seen in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك: وآمنهم من خوف: معناه من الجذام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The indefinite hunger and fear indicate severity: the journeys relieved prior famine and God protected them from the Elephant army or being seized on their routes.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والتنكير في جوع وخوف لشدتهما

rows.speaker: الجمهور والمسيبي عن نافع
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce the n of min openly before kh, whereas al-Musayyibi from Nafi hides it; hiding also occurs before ayn and is a known Arabic dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: من خوف، بإظهار النون عند الخاء، والمسيبي عن نافع: بإخفائها

rows.speaker: ابن الأسلت
rows.claim: The poet addresses Quraysh, urging prayer and touching the Kaaba's corners while recalling God's favor and rescue from the Elephant force.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأسلت يخاطب قريشا

rows.speaker: ابن الأسلت
rows.claim: His poem tells Quraysh to worship their Lord and touch the Kaaba's pillars, recalling their deliverance when the Lord's hosts turned back the Elephant army.
rows.anchor: فقوموا فصلوا ربكم وتمسحوا ... بأركان هذا البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naḥr is the camel's throat-cutting blow with a sharp instrument that causes death.
rows.anchor: انحر: أمر من النحر، وهو ضرب النحر للإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar means without descendants and derives from cutting off; it can describe a severed tail.
rows.anchor: الأبتر: الذي لا عقب له، والبتر: القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ziyad's speech was called al-batra because he omitted praise of God and blessings on the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وخطب زياد خطبته البتراء، لأنه لم يحمد فيها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abātir can mean one who cuts off kinship; the Batriyya Zaydis take their name from al-Mughira ibn Saʿd's nickname al-Abtar.
rows.anchor: ورجل أباتر، بضم الهمزة: الذي يقطع رحمه

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Most authorities call the sura Meccan; Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada are reported to call it Medinan.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في المشهور، وقول الجمهور: مدنية في قول الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura answers four vices in the preceding sura: stinginess with abundant gift, neglect of prayer with prayer, showing off with devotion to God, and withholding charity with sacrifice meat given away.
rows.anchor: قابل في هذه السورة البخل ب إنا أعطيناك الكوثر، والسهو في الصلاة بقوله: فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation concerns al-As ibn Wa'il, who called the Prophet abtar because he had no surviving descendants and claimed his memory would end at death.
rows.anchor: ونزلت في العاصي بن وائل، كان يسمي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأبتر

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وطلحة وابن محيصن والزعفراني
rows.claim: The majority read aʿṭaynāka with ʿayn; Hasan, Talha, Ibn Muhaysin, and al-Zafarani read anṭaynāka with nūn, also reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أعطيناك بالعين والحسن وطلحة وابن محيصن والزعفراني

rows.speaker: التبريزي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrizi says anṭaynāka is a dialect of ancient Arab Quraysh and cites Prophetic expressions using forms from that dialect.
rows.anchor: قال التبريزي: هي لغة للعرب العاربة من أولى قريش

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي وأبو زكريا التبرزي
rows.claim: They say if n replaces ʿayn as the dialect's regular counterpart, that is acceptable; if it is claimed as a morphological substitution, each form is instead an independent root.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفضل الرازي وأبو زكريا التبرزي: أبدل من العين نونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among twenty-six interpretations of Kawthar, the soundest is the Prophet's explanation that it is a river in Paradise with golden banks, jewel bed, fragrant soil, and water sweeter than honey and whiter than snow; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: والصحيح هو ما فسره به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In Muslim's report the Prophet calls Kawthar abundant good and a river promised by his Lord, with his community's basin and vessels as numerous as stars.
rows.anchor: قال: نهر وعدنيه ربي عليه خير كثير هو حوض ترد عليه أمتي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets Kawthar as abundant good; Ibn Jubayr says a Paradise river is one instance of that good.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الكوثر: الخير الكثير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets Kawthar as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الكوثر: القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عباس ويمان بن وثاب
rows.claim: They interpret Kawthar as the abundance of the Prophet's companions and followers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن عباس ويمان بن وثاب: كثرة الأصحاب والأتباع

rows.speaker: هلال بن يساف
rows.claim: Hilal ibn Yasaf interprets Kawthar as divine unity.
rows.anchor: وقال هلال بن يساف: هو التوحيد

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq describes it as light in the Prophet's heart guiding him to God and detaching him from everything else.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق: نور قلبه دله على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عكرمة والحسن بن الفضل وابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ikrima says prophethood, Hasan ibn al-Fadl ease in Qur'an and law, and Ibn Kaysan altruistic preference.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: النبوة. وقال الحسن بن الفضل: تيسير القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These interpretations should be understood as examples, not mutually exclusive definitions that confine Kawthar to one blessing.
rows.anchor: وينبغي حمل هذه الأقوال على التمثيل، لا أن الكوثر منحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar follows the intensive pattern fawʿal from abundance and means an exceptionally abundant amount.
rows.anchor: والكوثر فوعل من الكثرة، وهو المفرط الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent command to pray covers both obligatory and voluntary prayers.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن فصل أمر بالصلاة يدخل فيها المكتوبات والنوافل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The sacrifice command refers to the sacrificial camel, pilgrimage offering, and festival sacrifices; as there was no jihad then, these two acts were commanded.
rows.anchor: والنحر: نحر الهدي والنسك والضحايا، قاله الجمهور ولم يكن في ذلك الوقت جهاد

rows.speaker: أنس وقتادة
rows.claim: Anas and Qatada report that the Prophet sacrificed on Eid before prayer and was then ordered to pray before sacrificing.
rows.anchor: قال أنس: كان ينحر يوم الأضحى قبل الصلاة، فأمر أن يصلي وينحر

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the verse came at Hudaybiyya, commanding prayer and sacrifice of the pilgrimage offering; on this account it is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: نزلت وقت صلح الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For your Lord distinguishes the Prophet's worship from the Quraysh rites of clapping and whistling and sacrificing to idols.
rows.anchor: حيث كانت صلاتهم مكاء وتصدية، ونحرهم للأصنام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets the command as placing the right hand over the left at the chest during prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن علي، رضي الله تعالى عنه: صل لربك وضع يمينك على شمالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to raise the hands at the opening of prayer near the chest.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ارفع يديك في استفتاح صلاتك عند نحرك

rows.speaker: عطية وعكرمة
rows.claim: They interpret the prayer as dawn prayer at Muzdalifa and the sacrifice as occurring at Mina.
rows.anchor: وعن عطية وعكرمة: هي صلاة الفجر بجمع، والنحر بمنى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the command as sitting upright between the prostrations until the chest shows.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: استو بين السجدتين جالسا حتى يبدو نحرك

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abu al-Ahwas interprets it as facing the qibla with one's chest.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص: استقبل القبلة بنحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaniʾ means hater; al-As ibn Wa'il was identified earlier, while another opinion names Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: إن شانئك: أي مبغضك، تقدم أنه العاصي بن وائل. وقيل: أبو جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After Ibrahim died, Abu Jahl reportedly said Muhammad was cut off; the verse answered him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما مات إبراهيم ابن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: شمر بن عطية
rows.claim: Shamir ibn Atiyya identifies the hater as ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt.
rows.anchor: وقال شمر بن عطية: هو عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says abtar here means lowly and humiliated.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الأبتر هنا يراد به الحقير الذليل

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن عباس
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce shaniʾaka with alif, while Ibn Abbas reads shaynaka without it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: شانئك بالألف وابن عباس: شينك بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although grammatical analyses vary, the author prefers huwa as a separating pronoun: the Prophet's enemy alone is truly cut off, while the Prophet's remembrance and legacy endure.
rows.anchor: والأحسن الأعرف في المعنى أن يكون فصلا، أي هو المنفرد بالبتر

rows.speaker: الجمهور وقتادة
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan according to most authorities; Qatada is reported to regard it as Medinan.
rows.anchor: هذه مكية في قول الجمهور. وروي عن قتادة أنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion reports Quraysh offering wealth, marriage, and leadership, or alternating years of worship; the sura disavows them and says the bargain will never occur.
rows.anchor: طلبوا منه أن يعبد آلهتهم سنة ويعبدوا إلهه سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command say shows that Muhammad speaks by God's order; addressing these powerful opponents directly in their gathering with a contemptuous label signals divine protection.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: قل دليل على أنه مأمور بذلك من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are a specified group who made the offer, including al-Walid, al-As, al-Aswad, the two sons of Khalaf, Abu Jahl, and peers; their dying unbelievers fulfilled the warning.
rows.anchor: والكافرون ناس مخصوصون، وهم الذين قالوا له تلك المقالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation treats the repeated clauses as emphatic repetition, cutting off the disbelievers' hopes and confirming that they will die unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها للتوكيد. فقوله: ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم توكيد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash avoids redundancy by assigning the four clauses distinct times: present, following year, and future on each side.
rows.anchor: فقال الأخفش: المعنى لا أعبد الساعة ما تعبدون

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes the first two ma forms as relative pronouns and the latter two as verbal nouns, contrasting doubtful worship with worship grounded in certainty.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: ما في الأوليين بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the later clause clarifies that Muhammad will never worship their objects, and the final clause forecloses their future belief, like the decree about Noah's people but limited to named people here.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لما كان قوله: لا أعبد محتملا أن يراد به الآن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari interprets la as future negation and ma as present negation, so the proposal to worship each other's deity in future is denied.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لا أعبد، أريدت به العبادة فيما يستقبل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads the next clause as denying any past worship of their idols, then argues they could not expect future worship from Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم: أي وما كنت قط عابدا فيما سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Zamakhshari's absolute tense rule for la and ma: those particles usually, not invariably, indicate the tenses he assigns, as grammatical authorities show.
rows.anchor: فليس بصحيح، بل ذلك غالب فيهما لا متحتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle governing ma ʿabadtum cannot denote the past here; the author notes this is not the permissive past usage of al-Kisaʾi and Hisham.
rows.anchor: لأن عابدا اسم فاعل قد عمل فيما عبدتم، فلا يفسر بالماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the same reason, ʿabidun governing ma aʿbud cannot mean what they worshipped while Muhammad worshipped.
rows.anchor: فعابدون قد أعمله فيما أعبد، فلا يفسر بالماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Zamakhshari's suggestion irreverent and wrong: Muhammad remained a monotheist, avoided their idols, and performed Abrahamic rites at the House.
rows.anchor: فسوء أدب منه على منصب النبوة، وهو أيضا غير صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God and monotheism are among the greatest acts of worship, as the author reads the purpose in 51:56 as knowing God.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads la as mostly negating the future, then uses the active participle to negate the present on both sides; the balanced clauses mean neither side worships the other's deity, and their unbelief is divinely decreed.
rows.anchor: والذي أختاره في هذه الجمل أنه أولا: نفى عبادته في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ma in the contrast is justified by parallelism even if ma normally does not denote a rational being; some scholars attributed to Sibawayh permit that usage directly.
rows.anchor: لأن المقابلة يسوغ فيها ما لا يسوغ مع الانفراد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: For those who say ma cannot refer to rational beings, parallelism permits its use here for God.
rows.anchor: وهذا على مذهب من يقول: أن ما لا تقع على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing formula contrasts their associationism with his monotheism and completes the disavowal; the earlier clauses foreground his own separation, then address them in a truce-like manner.
rows.anchor: لكم شرككم ولي توحيدي، وهذا غاية في التبرؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conciliatory closing is abrogated by the sword verse; Salam retains the final ya of dini in both connection and pause, unlike the seven readers.
rows.anchor: وهي منسوخة بآية السيف. وقرأ سلام: ديني بياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take ma as a verbal noun in the final clauses or throughout.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما مصدرية في قوله: ما أعبد. وقيل: فيها جميعها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari treats ma as a description: I worship no falsehood, and you worship no truth.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: المراد الصفة، كأنه قيل: لا أعبد الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Medinan, revealed on return from Khaybar, and the Prophet lived two years afterward.
rows.anchor: هذه مدنية، نزلت منصرفه صلى الله عليه وسلم من غزوة خيبر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says it came during the middle days of tashriq at Mina on the Farewell Pilgrimage, about eighty days before the Prophet's death.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: نزلت في أوسط أيام التشريق بمنى في حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where the prior sura offered a truce, this one threatens opponents with God's victory, Mecca's conquest, the collapse of idolatry, and the triumph of Islam.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في قوله: لكم دينكم موادعة، جاء في هذه بما يدل على تخويفهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والحوفي
rows.claim: They make idha governed by tasbih and see the prior announcement of the future conquest as a sign of prophecy.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: إذا منصوب بسبح، وهو لما يستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects governing idha by fasabbih because the answer's fa blocks that verb; he says the verb after it governs the conditional noun, despite another common grammatical position.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح إعمال فسبح في إذا لأجل الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasr means aid and victory over an enemy, while fath means conquest; the omitted objects are apparently victory for the Prophet and believers and conquests including Mecca, Taif, the Hijaz, and Yemen.
rows.anchor: والنصر: الإعانة والإظهار على العدو، والفتح: فتح البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrower view specifies victory over Quraysh and Mecca's conquest on 10 Ramadan in year eight, with ten thousand emigrants and Helpers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصره صلى الله عليه وسلم على قريش وفتح مكة

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن كثير
rows.claim: Most readers use the active form yadkhuluna; Ibn Kathir in one transmission reads it passively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يدخلون مبنيا للفاعل وابن كثير في رواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's religion is Islam, and crowds means whole tribes entering together after individuals and pairs had entered earlier.
rows.anchor: أفواجا أي جماعات كثيرة، كانت تدخل فيه القبيلة بأسرها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: After Mecca's conquest, Arabs realized that resisting the sacred people was impossible because God had protected them from the Elephant army.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: لما فتح عليه الصلاة والسلام مكة، أقبلت العرب بعضها على بعض

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: He says no Arab remained an unbeliever when the Prophet died; all entered Islam after Hunayn, some coming personally and others sending delegates.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر: لم يمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي العرب رجل كافر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes the people as Arab idolaters but doubts that the Christians of Banu Taghlib ever converted in the Prophet's life, saying they paid jizya.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والمراد، والله أعلم، العرب عبدة الأوثان

rows.speaker: مقاتل وعكرمة
rows.claim: They identify the people as Yemenis, with seven hundred men among the delegation.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل وعكرمة: المراد بالناس أهل اليمن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the crowds as Arab delegations arriving between Mecca's conquest and the Prophet's death.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: وفود العرب، وكان دخولهم بين فتح مكة وموته

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hufi analyzes afwaj as a broken plural and explains its form by the unusual pattern of hollow nouns; the author corrects that the regular pattern here is afʿal, with afʿul exceptional.
rows.anchor: قال الحوفي: وقياس جمعه أفوج، ولكن استثقلت الضمة على الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwajan is circumstantial; dakhiluna can also be the second object if raʾayta means knowing, while the author questions Zamakhshari's unsupported claim that raʾayta means recognized.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إما على الحال على أن أرأيت بمعنى أبصرت أو عرفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should glorify God while praising him for victory, conquest, and people's conversion; every good act of Muslims accrues to his account.
rows.anchor: فسبح بحمد ربك: أي ملتبسا بحمده على هذه النعم التي خولكها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that near the end of his life the Prophet often said, Glory to you, O God, with your praise; I seek your forgiveness and repent to you.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر قبل موته أن يقول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says joining forgiveness to glorification completes religion through obedience and avoidance of sin, models humility for the community despite infallibility, and makes seeking forgiveness worship in itself.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والأمر بالاستغفار مع التسبيح تكميل للأمر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said he sought God's forgiveness one hundred times by day and by night.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إني لأستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة مائة مرة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet understood the sura as announcing his approaching death; the Companions rejoiced while al-Abbas wept, explaining that it foretold his death, which the Prophet affirmed.
rows.anchor: وقد علم هو صلى الله عليه وسلم من هذه السورة دنو أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being ever accepting of repentance gives great hope to those who seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: إنه كان توابا: فيه ترجئة عظيمة للمستغفرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haṭab is wood, and saying someone carries wood against another means slandering that person; jīd means neck.
rows.anchor: الحطب معروف، ويقال: فلان يحطب على فلان إذا وشى عليه. الجيد: العنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad is a rope of palm fiber; Abu al-Fath specifies the dwarf palm, Ibn Zayd a Yemeni tree, and it can also be camel hide or hair.
rows.anchor: المسد: الحبل من ليف، وقال أبو الفتح: ليف المقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited rajaz line uses masad for a tightly twisted cord, and the related adjective means strongly twisted.
rows.anchor: قال الراجز: ومسد أمر من أيانق ورجل ممسود الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the prior sura's mass conversion, this one describes Abu Lahab as a loser who stayed outside the faith embraced by Mecca.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها دخول الناس في دين الله تعالى، أتبع بذكر من لم يدخل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جبير وعطاء ويمان بن رياب
rows.claim: They gloss tabbat as failed, lost, perished, strayed, or emptied of all good; the author says these meanings are close.
rows.anchor: وهنا قال ابن عباس: خابت، وقتادة: خسرت، وابن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruin is attributed to the hands because actions are mostly done with them, though the true object is the self, as in 22:10.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الهلاك إلى اليدين، لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Abu Lahab took a stone in his hands to throw at the Messenger, explaining the specific attribution.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أخذ بيديه حجرا ليرمي به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is an imprecation in tabbat followed by a report that it came to pass; Abd Allah's wa-qad tabb supports this.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التب دعاء، وتب: إخبار بحصول ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet called relatives and Quraysh to warn them of punishment; Abu Lahab cursed the gathering, after which this sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's personal name was Abd al-Uzza; the author identifies his family relation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأبو لهب اسمه عبد العزى

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن وابن كثير
rows.claim: They read Abu Lahab with a silent h; the other seven readers open it, while the fixed rhyme in dhata lahab keeps the opening vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وابن كثير: أبي لهب بسكون الهاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls the silent h a change in proper names, like the altered pronunciation of Shams Malik.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهو من تغيير الأعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says that explanation is not necessary: Abu Lahab is normally pronounced with an open h, and Shams Malik could simply have been named Shams from a plural form.
rows.anchor: بل يمكن أن يكون مسمى بشمس المنقول من شمس الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several explanations are offered for the kunya: his bright looks, its greater currency than his name, his destiny in fire, or its lower rank than a personal name; the last is linked to naming prophets rather than giving them kunyas.
rows.anchor: قيل: وكني بأبي لهب لحسنه وإشراق وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent ma is negative: neither inherited wealth nor personal earnings, livestock, offspring, or trade profits could benefit Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في ما أغنى عنه ماله نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes ma an interrogative in the accusative, asking what his wealth could avail.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما استفهاما في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma in wa-ma kasab is apparently relative but may be a verbal noun; if the first ma is interrogative, the second may be as well.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في قوله: وما كسب موصولة، وأجيز أن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says what Abu Lahab gained was his child, with a report that a man's child is his earning.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: وما كسب ولده

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the gain as Abu Lahab's evil work against the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك: وما كسب هو عمله الخبيث في عداوة الرسول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it refers to the deeds Abu Lahab thought would benefit him.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: وعمله الذي ظن أنه منه على شيء

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: They read sayuṣla passively, with ḍamma on y and a silent ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق: سيصلى بضم الياء وسكون الصاد

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba reads ḥāmilata al-ḥaṭab on the active participle pattern as a genitive construction.
rows.anchor: وأبو قلابة: حاملة الحطب على وزن فاعلة مضافا

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar and others lightly pronounce the h in wa-imraʾatuhu.
rows.anchor: واختلس حركة الهاء في وامرأته أبو عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the majority's nominative reading, ḥammāla can be a predicate of an omitted subject or an adjective of the wife.
rows.anchor: وحمالة في قراءة الجمهور خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أو صفة لامرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another nominative parse makes the wife a new subject and ḥammāla its predicate.
rows.anchor: وأجازوا في قراءة الرفع أن يكون وامرأته مبتدأ، وحمالة

rows.speaker: أبو لهب
rows.claim: A report says Abu Lahab offered to ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew's message proved true.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أنه كان يقول: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبو حيوة وابن مقسم وعباس
rows.claim: Reported readings include wa-ma iktasaba with an added t, passive sayuṣalla, and diminutive or hamzated forms for wife; another reading gives hammālata with tanwin and a preposition before al-haṭab.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: وما اكتسب بتاء الافتعال

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read sayasla actively, wife in the nominative, and hammālata in the intensive pattern; the future sīn marks certain promised punishment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سيصلى بفتح الياء وسكون الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife is attached to the hidden subject of sayasla, separated by its object and modifier; hammāla can be a predicate of an omitted subject or an adjective, while accusative marks censure.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النصب، انتصب على الذم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wife, Umm Jamil, sister of Abu Sufyan, literally carried thornwood to lay in the Prophet's and his Companions' path and injure them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها كانت تحمل الحطب، أي ما فيه شوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the reported wood-carrying as gossip that kindles conflict among people.
rows.anchor: بالنميمة، ويقال للمشاء بها: يحمل الحطب بين الناس

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem uses carrying wet wood as an image of gossip and added malice, since wetness signals smoke.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: من البيض لم يصطد على ظهر لأمة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says she carried sins and misdeeds, using the Qur'anic image of people carrying their burdens on their backs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: حمالة الخطايا والذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes al-haṭab as a plural for those who carry, meaning she drove wrongdoers into further wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحطب جمع حاطب، كحارس وحرس

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير ومجاهد وسفيان
rows.claim: They take the rope as a metaphor for an iron chain in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال عروة بن الزبير ومجاهد وسفيان: استعارة، والمراد سلسلة من حديد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the rope as a necklace of cowrie shells.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قلادة من ودع

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب والحسن وابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says an expensive jewel necklace she vowed to spend against Muhammad; Hasan says beads, and Ibn Atiyya sees the rope wording as an ill omen reflecting her wicked activity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: قلادة فاخرة من جوهر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari reads the rope literally as a degrading woodcutter's burden tied around her neck, mocking a wealthy, noble couple; he also offers a Hell image matching her earthly actions with firewood and chains.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والمعنى في جيدها حبل مما مسد من الحبال

rows.speaker: الفضل بن العباس بن عتبة بن أبي لهب
rows.claim: A poem attributed to him rebukes someone for insulting him as a carrier of wood and asserts his mother's noble ancestry.
rows.anchor: ولقد عير بعض الناس الفضل بن العباس بن عتبة بن أبي لهب بحمالة الحطب

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line explicitly equates carrying wood with tale-bearing in both ease and anger.
rows.anchor: وقال الراجز: إن بني الأرزم حمالو الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When she heard the sura, Umm Jamil came to Abu Bakr and the Prophet with a pestle, threatening the man who insulted her; God prevented her from seeing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وبيدها فهر، فقالت: بلغني أن صاحبك هجاني

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said angels had screened him from her sight; the report adds that she died strangled by her rope and Abu Lahab died of smallpox seven nights after Badr.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لقد حجبتني عنها ملائكة فما رأتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣamad is on the faʿl pattern with passive meaning, from turning to someone: the master whom people approach for needs and who suffices them; poetry supports the usage.
rows.anchor: الصمد: فعل بمعنى مفعول من صمد إليه إذا قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufuʾ means an equal or counterpart.
rows.anchor: الكفو: النظير

rows.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وعكرمة وعطاء ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: These authorities consider the sura Meccan; Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Abu al-Aliya, and al-Dahhak consider it Medinan.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول عبد الله والحسن وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Abu Lahab and the idolaters, this sura explicitly affirms monotheism and refutes idol worship, dualism, trinitarianism, and other beliefs that oppose it.
rows.anchor: جاءت هذه السورة مصرحة بالتوحيد، رادة على عباد الأوثان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews asked Muhammad to describe and establish his Lord's lineage, prompting the sura.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، أن اليهود قالوا: يا محمد صف لنا ربك وانسبه

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says leaders of the confederates asked him to state his Lord's lineage, prompting the sura.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي العالية، قال قادة الأحزاب: انسب لنا ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If that occasion is authentic, huwa refers back to the Lord: say, He is Allah, my Lord; ahad is a second predicate.
rows.anchor: فإن صح هذا السبب، كان هو ضميرا عائدا على الرب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari parses ahad either as an appositive to Allah or as the predicate of huwa.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وأحد بدل من قوله: الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without that occasion, huwa is the pronoun of the matter and the following sentence its predicate; ahad means uniquely one in essence and attributes, indivisible in every respect.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يصح السبب، فهو ضمير الأمر، والشأن مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza of ahad replaces waw, a rare open-hamza substitution, like anāh for wanāh.
rows.anchor: وهمزة أحد هذا بدل من واو، وإبدال الهمزة مفتوحة من الواو قليل

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes aḥad, which does not take number or dual forms, from wāḥid, which does; he reserves aḥad for God, though the author notes that number words contradict the claim.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب: بين واحد وأحد فرق، الواحد يدخله العدد

rows.speaker: أبان بن عثمان وزيد بن علي ونصر بن عاصم وابن سيرين والحسن
rows.claim: A large set of readers deletes tanwin before Allah in ahad Allah; the author says this occurs in Arabic, especially poetry, and cites examples.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبان بن عثمان، وزيد بن علي، ونصر بن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line supports deletion of tanwin before Allah in the reading ahad Allah.
rows.anchor: عمرو الذي هشم الثريد لقومه الله الصمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah al-Ṣamad is best read as a standalone subject-predicate clause, like successive descriptions of Zayd; another view makes al-Ṣamad an adjective with the next clause as predicate.
rows.anchor: والأفصح أن تكون هذه جملا مستقلة بالأخبار على سبيل الاستئناف

rows.speaker: الشعبي ويمان بن رياب
rows.claim: They define al-Ṣamad as one who neither eats nor drinks.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي، ويمان بن رياب: هو الذي لا يأكل ولا يشرب

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb explains al-Ṣamad by the following clause, He neither begets nor is begotten.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: يفسره ما بعده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says al-Ṣamad is solid and without a cavity, supported by a poetic use of muṣmat.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الصمد: المصمت الذي لا جوف له

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says lexicographers agree al-Ṣamad is the supreme master with none above him, whom people approach for their needs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: لا خلاف بين أهل اللغة أن الصمد هو السيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says God does not beget because he has no consort of his kind, citing 6:101; he is not begotten because every begotten being is created and embodied, while God is eternal and no one equals him.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: لم يلد، لأنه لا يجانس حتى تكون له من جنسه صاحبة

rows.speaker: حمزة وحفص وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: The readings vary the vowels and hamza of kufu: Hamza and Hafs use a silent f with ḍamma on k, Hamza keeps hamza while Hafs changes it to waw; the others have both vowels and hamza, with several readers easing or deleting it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحفص: بضم الكاف وإسكان الفاء، وهمز حمزة

rows.speaker: سليمان بن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: He reads kifā with kasra on k, open f, and a long vowel, matching the cited line meaning that God has no equal.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سليمان بن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس: كفاء بكسر الكاف

rows.speaker: مكي سيبويه والمبرد وابن عطية
rows.claim: Makkī attributes to Sibawayh a preference for a fronted adverb as predicate; al-Mubarrad objects from this verse, while the author answers that Sibawayh allowed either parse and Ibn Atiyya also permits a circumstantial parse.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي سيبويه: يختار أن يكون الظرف خبرا إذا قدمه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari asks why the adverb is fronted despite eloquence normally delaying a nonessential one; he answers that the divine counterpart relation is the focus.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: الكلام العربي الفصيح أن يؤخر الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase lahu is incomplete and cannot be the predicate; it is attached to kufuwan and fronted for emphasis, leaving the noun for the rhyme.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة ليست من هذا الباب، وذلك أن قوله: ولم يكن له كفوا أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This analysis invalidates Makkī's and others' parse of lahu as predicate and kufuwan as a circumstantial accusative, and makes Zamakhshari's question and answer irrelevant.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الذي قررناه يبطل إعراب مكي وغيره أن له الخبر

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh's discussion concerns a complete adverb that can be predicate or adjunct; either placement is good Arabic, with order depending on the intended parse.
rows.anchor: سيبويه إنما تكلم في هذا الظرف الذي يصلح أن يكون خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī and Zamakhshari misread Sibawayh's example: it concerns a complete adverb used as an adjunct, comparable to lahu here, not as a predicate.
rows.anchor: فقد مثل بالآية الكريمة. قلت: هذا الذي أوقع مكيا والزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without kufuwan, wa-lam yakun lahu ahad is not a complete sentence; the negation targets equality, with lahu attached to it, meaning no one is God's equal.
rows.anchor: بل أنت ترى أن النفي لم يتسلط إلا على الخبر الذي هو كفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports describe this sura's merit, including that it equals a third of the Qur'an; the scholars discussed this elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في فضل هذه السورة أحاديث كثيرة، ومنها أنها تعدل ثلث القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq has the pattern faʿl with passive meaning; the author says exegetes' interpretations will follow.
rows.anchor: الفلق: فعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaba can describe night darkening, the sun setting, or punishment arriving; a poem illustrates punishment descending.
rows.anchor: وقب الليل: أظلم والشمس: غابت، والعذاب: حل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya defines nafth as blowing without spittle.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عطية: وقيل: نفخ بريق معه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari allows nafth to include spittle with the blowing; the Luwaamis author says blowing without spittle is ruqya, whereas with spittle it is tafl.
rows.anchor: قاله الزمخشري. وقال صاحب اللوامح: شبه النفخ من الفم في الرقية

rows.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة وجابر وكريب عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: These authorities consider the sura Meccan; Ibn Abbas in another report, Qatada, and a group say Medinan, which the author deems correct.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة وجابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion of the two protective suras is the magic of Labid ibn al-Aʿsam against the Prophet; eleven knots in a palm spathe were undone as the verses were recited, relieving him.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزول المعوذتين قصة سحر لبيد بن الأعصم اليهودي رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining divinity in the preceding sura, this one teaches refuge in God from evils across the world's created kinds.
rows.anchor: ولما شرح أمر الإلهية في السورة قبلها، شرح ما يستعاذ منه بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله ومجاهد وقتادة وابن جبير والقرطبي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They interpret falaq as dawn, supported by proverbs and poetry.
rows.anchor: والفلق: الصبح، قاله ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes falaq as everything God splits open: earth, plants, mountains, clouds, wombs, seeds, and more.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفلق: كلما يفلقه الله تعالى، كالأرض والنبات والجبال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: They identify falaq as a pit in Hell; Abu Hurayra transmits this from the Prophet, and some say it is a valley.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين: الفلق: جب في جهنم

rows.speaker: بعض الصحابة
rows.claim: Some Companions call it a house in Hell whose opening makes all its inhabitants cry from the intense heat.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الصحابة: بيت في جهنم، إذا فتح صاح جميع أهل النار

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers attach sharr to the general ma, covering every possible source of harm, accountable or not and animate or inanimate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: من شر ما خلق، بإضافة شر إلى ما

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Amr ibn Ubayd and some Muʿtazilites read sharr with tanwin and take ma as negative, reflecting the false claim that God did not create evil; the author says the reading can instead make ma an appositional clarification with an ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقرأ عمرو بن عبيد، وبعض المعتزلة القائلين بأن الله تعالى لم يخلق الشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: They interpret the ghasik as night when its darkness falls and reaches people; Zamakhshari amplifies this as dense, pervasive darkness and cites 17:78.
rows.anchor: والغاسق: الليل، ووقب: أظلم ودخل على الناس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes ghasik as cold, dangerous at night when devils, vermin, snakes, and assailants emerge.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو الليل لأنه أبرد من النهار

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب وابن شهاب والقتبي
rows.claim: Other views identify ghasik as day entering night, the setting sun, or the moon eclipsed in its sheath.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: النهار دخل في الليل. وقال ابن شهاب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet looked at the moon and told Aisha to seek refuge from it when it entered, calling it al-fasiq.
rows.anchor: نظر صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى القمر فقال: يا عائشة، نعوذ بالله من هذا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another prophetic report identifies ghasik as a star.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الغاسق النجم»

rows.speaker: ابن زيد عن العرب
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that Arabs use ghasik for the Pleiades when they set, when illnesses and plague flare; another view says a biting snake, whose venom flows.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد عن العرب: الغاسق: الثريا إذا سقطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naffathat may mean women, souls, or groups of sorceresses who tie knots in strings and blow incantations over them.
rows.anchor: والنفاثات: النساء، أو النفوس، أو الجماعات السواحر

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وابن عمر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Readings include al-naffathat by most, a version with ḍamma on n from Hasan, al-nafithat from Ibn Umar and others, and al-nafthat without alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: النفاثات والحسن: بضم النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge concerns harm God brings about when sorceresses perform their acts.
rows.anchor: والاستعاذة من شرهن هو ما يصيب الله تعالى به من الشر عند فعلهن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari proposes that the women are scheming seductresses or women who enchant men with displayed beauty; the author says the reported magic occasion refutes this.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزول هاتين المعوذتين ينفي ما تأوله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya describes magic knots tied on threads in the victim's name and reports a reliable witness saw knots prevent foals from nursing until a knot was undone.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وهذا النفث هو على عقد تعقد في خيوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and envy become sources of harm when their effects emerge; hidden envy alone pains the envier, while Zamakhshari also interprets the refuge as protection from the sin and ugliness of displayed envy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الغاسق والحاسد بالطرف، لأنه إذا لم يدخل الليل لا يكون منسوبا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura first generalizes evil, then singles out hidden harms; ghasik and hasid are indefinite because only some nights and envying people cause harm, while naffathat is definite because every sorceress is evil.
rows.anchor: وعرف النفاثات، لأن كل نفاثة شريرة، وكل غاسق لا يكون فيه الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some envy is praiseworthy when directed at good deeds, as in the report that envy is allowed only in two cases and the cited poetry.
rows.anchor: ورب حسد محمود، وهو الحسد في الخيرات، ومنه: لا حسد إلا في اثنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying about the envious person's eye alludes to this five-verse sura as protection from the evil eye.
rows.anchor: وقول المنظور إليه للحاسد، إذا نظر الخمس على عينيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sura was revealed with the preceding one; God is called Lord of people because people seek their own master when endangered by the whisperer who harms their hearts.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الرب إلى الناس، لأن الاستعاذة من شر الموسوس في صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes King of people and God of people two attributes; Zamakhshari instead treats them as appositives, each narrowing the description until only God is uniquely deity.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ملك الناس إله الناس صفتان. وقال الزمخشري: هما عطفا بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions whether apposition can be repeated for one antecedent and notes that apposition is normally a noun, not an adjective.
rows.anchor: وعطف البيان المشهور أنه يكون بالجوامد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the repeated explicit word people suits explanatory apposition, rather than replacing the noun with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: قلت: لأن عطف البيان للبيان، فكان مظنة للإظهار دون الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswas may be Satan's name or the soul's forbidden desires; khannas is one who retreats and hides, as Satan does when God is remembered, while desires retreat through faith, angelic prompting, and shame.
rows.anchor: والوسواس، قالوا: اسم من أسماء الشيطان؟ والوسواس أيضا: ما يوسوس به شهوات النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From jinn and people may mean devils and human souls, or Satan and human tempters; 6:112 describes human and jinn devils exchanging deceptive speech.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن من الإنس شياطين، ومن الجن شياطين

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr asks a man whether he sought refuge from human devils.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ذر لرجل: هل تعوذت من شياطين الإنس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls waswas a verbal noun like zalzala, with the kasra form as verbal noun; Satan is named by his craft or as possessor of whispers. The author notes he has disputed this account of 99:1.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الوسواس اسم بمعنى الوسوسة، كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun may be genitive as an adjective or nominative or accusative as a term of insult.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في الذي الجر على الصفة، والرفع والنصب على الشتم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Min may be partitive, describing whisperers as some of jinn and some of people, or it may be governed by yuwaswis to mark the source of their whispering.
rows.anchor: ومن في من الجنة والناس للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because religious harm from whispering exceeds worldly harm, this refuge invokes three divine attributes; refuge from the three worldly evils in the preceding sura invokes only Lord.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت مضرة الدين، وهي آفة الوسوسة، أعظم من مضرة الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: At bedtime the Prophet cupped his hands, blew into them, recited the declaration of unity and the two protective suras, then wiped his body three times starting with head and face.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا آوى إلى فراشه جمع كفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan without dispute; it has eleven verses by the Kufans, ten by the Hijazis, and eight by Basran and Syrian counts, and its relation to the previous sura is obvious.
rows.anchor: سورة القارعة مكية بلا خلاف وآيها احدى عشرة آية في الكوفي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators identify al-Qariʿa as the Resurrection itself, from the first trumpet blast through judgment among creatures.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أنها القيامة نفسها ومبدؤها النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views identify it as the sound of the trumpet or, according to al-Dahhak, Hell with its raging and roaring; the author rejects the latter view.
rows.anchor: وقيل صوت النفخة وقال الضحاك هي النار ذات التغيظ والزفير وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In any case, qariʿa derives from forceful striking that produces a loud sound, and the grammar parallels the discussion of 69:1-3.
rows.anchor: وأياً ما كان فهي من القرع وهو الضرب بشدة بحيث يحصل منه صوت شديد

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: Isa reads al-qariʿata in the accusative, understood with an omitted imperative: remember the Calamity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى القارعة بالنصب وخرج على أنه بإضمار فعل
